title: Add tracing spans to Rust async functions — 3 turns
description: Add tracing instrumentation to existing async handlers. Turn 1: add #[instrument]. Turn 2: add structured fields. Turn 3: add test that captures spans.

files.Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "tracing-example"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
tracing = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }

[dev-dependencies]
tracing-test = "0.2"

task_spec.prompt: Add `#[instrument]` to `process_request` in `src/lib.rs`. The `instrument` macro is already imported from `tracing`. Add the attribute just above `pub async fn process_request(request: Request)`. Run `cargo test --quiet`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now add structured fields to the span: change `#[instrument]` on `process_request` to `#[instrument(fields(request_id = request.id, user_id = request.user_id))]` to log the IDs. Also add `#[instrument(fields(action = %action))]` to `validate_action`. Run `cargo test --quiet` and fix any failures.
Run `cargo test --quiet` to verify everything including the traced_test. Fix any failures and confirm all 3 tests pass.
success_criteria: Structured fields include request_id and user_id
validate_action has instrument with action field
All 3 async tests pass including the traced_test
